title: How the show worked, no drummer, route and repertoire
summary: Band played silently as props to the dancer, blues and two-four tunes for her steps, matinee and night, the tour route.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: What about a drummer in Chicago? You didn't use any drummer then?

No. Well, no, I'll tell you. When we got to Chicago, they suggested that they wasn't going to use no drummer. You know? Yeah. They used a fat fella for a while, but they put him off. And they say he was too loud or something. He wasn't from here. He's not from here. When we got over there, we seen him, but he was from over there. So the manager suggested that we would make it without that. So we just used our six pieces. Yeah. And while she was dancing and singing and making them designs, you know, making them figures as if it was playing. We're not playing. We're only making a figure of what they're supposed to be playing. You know, people there. That's when we had our pictures taken in front of the stage. Before anyone would come in the show, well, we was only making a design so we can put that on the outside and that'll, you know, for the people, you know, for the people come, they'll look at these pictures on the outside. How come they get this? Well, the manager, he gave me one. And he gave the other fella one too, I believe. He said, well, Kepeda, as you're going home, he says, here's one of the pictures. So he gave me that one. That's what happened. Well, when the actual show was playing to the audience, where was the band then, Louis? Well, the band was on the stage like this, but they never had a drop scene. That's only, that drop scene is only to take our pictures. I see. You see? Now, when we're not playing, the drop scene is down, but it dropped behind us. And then we get on front of stage and then we start making our introduction or starting off with. I don't know if you heard that. Oh, yeah. I don't know if you heard that.
Yeah, yeah, just an Egyptian piece, Egyptian rag.

Then all at once, you see now this here would be up. And you see it would be halfway there when we're playing. And then when it was over here, that thing would be creeping. Creeping up. Then all at once, the second part. Clionette make that. See, and then it'll hit up there. And then she come out after that. And then we'd be. We'd break the time. We'd break the time. And fast part would bring the thing up in the hurry. Then she'd come out and dancing. And we'd be on the back of her. And she'd be in front of the stage. And she'd be cutting all them steps. Did she sing too or just the steps? Yeah, she could sing. Yeah, she could sing and she was good. Or she could cut some steps. What would the date on that begin? This here is May the 15th. May the 15th. May the 15th. May the 15th. May the 15th. She could sing. Yes, she could sing and she was good. Oh, she could cut some steps. What was the date on that again? This here is May the 15th, 1917. May the 15th, 1917.
Do you know any other numbers that you played for her, or did you have any other numbers by yourself?

Well, no, we all, we had what they called, we had other old pieces we used to play, the blues, old time blues like that. And let me see, there's another thing they called the tromboners. There's plenty of tromboneers like that. And then, somebody stole my gal and all that. You know, and all the more, and then she'd be cutting the steps and dancing. Then we'd put it in the two-fourth time. See? We'd make it through that so she could make her steps right. See? Nothing couldn't be slow because we wanted her to cut her steps. And after we'd come, when we'd go in, well, as a, it was always on the same show, but it wasn't our show. It was another troupe which was in us to make the show longer. See? When you see a show, Bill Bale and all of them comes out, it don't be one man got that. He put in to get there and make a big thing of it. Yeah. Now, they all got a different, different bosses, you know? Now, when they get, when she get off of that, then the other one, they come and shoot with their own band. See? That's the way. But this is her band and hers play. She'd make about three plays and then she's gone. We used to have matinee in the daytime, but an hour, or half an hour. And then, at night, we'd come on again and when we'd finish, somebody else would come right behind us. Then we'd gone. Get the train at 11 o'clock in the nighttime and go somewhere else. Cedar Rapids Highway, St. Louis, Missouri, somewhere in Chicago. Well, we was in, we started in Chicago. Well, we went to Cedar Rapids Highway, then we went and fell in St. Louis, Missouri, and we were supposed to go to another one. But we were supposed to go to different places at the same time. But when he said for me to go to California or Chicago, I mean New York, well I was home and I didn't care about going no more. But all them were good fellas, nice fellas, they played. And they had good bands. Now, of course, now, this here picture of my brothers, what I got in that frame there. And they said, my daddy, you can get up and see it.
